extracted.intended_audience: parties to ITC investigations, trade attorneys, patent owners/accused infringers, and interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Trade Commission (U.S. International Trade Commission) notice describing the Commission's determination to reconsider and modify remedial orders in an Investigation under section 337, including applicable legal authority, standards for petitions for reconsideration, and the scope of repair/replacement exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority for Commission determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority for the Commission's determination is contained in section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (19 U.S.C. 1337), and in Part 210 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 CFR part 210).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All determinations, remedial orders, and procedural actions in investigations under this docket are grounded in 19 U.S.C. 1337 and 19 CFR part 210; references to specific rules (e.g., 19 CFR 210.47) control petitionability and standards for reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission Rule 210.47 standard for petitions for reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for reconsideration must be 'confined to new questions raised by the determination or action ordered to be taken thereunder and upon which the petitioner had no opportunity to submit arguments.' (19 CFR 210.47)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet Rule 210.47's confinement-to-new-questions/No-opportunity-to-argue standard is a basis to deny a petition for reconsideration (see Commissioner Karpel's view that Peloton's Petition fails to meet the Rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of repair and service exemptions in remedial orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedial orders included repair and replacement exemptions, which included an exemption for parts necessary to service and repair covered products purchased by consumers prior to the date of the orders, and an exemption for covered products that are replacements for covered products purchased by consumers prior to the date of the orders, provided that replacement is pursuant to a warranty for the replaced article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing remedial orders, the Commission may expressly define exemptions to avoid undue harm to consumers—e.g., permitting import/use of parts for servicing products purchased before the order date and permitting warranty-based replacements only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond determination for remedial orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission imposed a bond of zero (0%) (i.e., no bond) in the remedial orders issued with the Final Determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission can set the percentage bond (including zero) attached to remedial relief during Presidential review; bond level is an explicit remedial parameter and may affect remedy implementation during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation of consumer harm during Presidential review period
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission determined that the mitigation of harm to U.S. consumers underlying the service and repair exemptions did not extend to U.S. consumers who have purchased or may purchase covered products during the Presidential review period, prompting sua sponte reconsideration and modification of remedial orders to reduce their impact on those consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When crafting or modifying remedial orders, the Commission evaluates whether exemptions adequately mitigate consumer harm during the Presidential review period; insufficient mitigation to consumers purchasing during that period can justify modification of remedial orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission authority/practice to act sua sponte to reconsider remedial orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission determined sua sponte to reconsider the remedial orders originally issued in this investigation and to issue orders modifying those remedial orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may on its own initiative revisit and modify previously issued remedial orders where it identifies considerations (e.g., consumer harm during review) warranting change; Commissioners may separately state concurrence or dissent and propose alternative modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement-based partial termination procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A joint, unopposed motion to partially terminate the investigation may be filed based on a settlement agreement (example: MIRROR and DISH filed a joint, unopposed motion to partially terminate the investigation as to MIRROR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties seeking termination of proceedings as to particular respondents or claims may file joint, unopposed motions based on settlement; the Commission will act on such motions and may terminate investigations in part accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of permissible service/repair exemption modification (Commissioner Karpel's view)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify remedial orders by extending the service and repair exemption to permit Respondents to import and use component parts for service and repair of damaged fitness devices that are or have been purchased by U.S. consumers during the Presidential review period, but do not permit Respondents to supply as a replacement the identical fitness device purchased by the consumer during this period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This articulates a narrower exemption approach: allow parts for repair of devices purchased during review but disallow replacing the full device that was purchased during the review period; reflects a balancing of consumer harm and remedial scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader replacement-exemption approach (Commissioner Schmidtlein's view)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner Schmidtlein would extend the exemption for replacement of the whole article in this case to include those that are not currently under warranty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An alternative remedial approach is to broaden replacement exemptions beyond warranty-limited replacements to include whole-article replacements even if the replaced article is no longer under warranty, to further mitigate consumer harm.
